entries.claim: Trustworthy online controlled experiments require predefined metrics, minimum detectable effect, sample size, randomisation checks and a decision rule before launch
entries.locator: Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments

entries.claim: Repeatedly checking results and stopping at the first significant p-value (peeking or optional stopping) inflates the actual type I error rate well above the nominal level, and requires sequential or always-valid methods
entries.locator: Johari et al. (2017), Proceedings of KDD
entries.notes: Supports the peeking section and figure

entries.claim: Two independent proportions are compared with a z statistic using the pooled proportion and the standard error sqrt(pbar(1-pbar)(1/n1+1/n2))
entries.locator: OpenStax, Introductory Statistics, comparing two proportions

entries.claim: The per-group sample size for comparing two proportions is approximately (z_{1-alpha/2} sqrt(2 pbar(1-pbar)) + z_{1-beta} sqrt(p1(1-p1)+p2(1-p2)))^2 / (p2-p1)^2
entries.locator: statsmodels power and sample size reference
entries.notes: Equation 1; the tabulated numbers are computed from it

entries.claim: For 850/10000 versus 920/10000 the pooled proportion is 0.0885, z is about 1.74 and the two-sided p is about 0.081; for a base rate of 0.085 with alpha 0.05 and power 0.80 the per-group sample sizes are about 50134, 12856, 5856, 3373 and 1569 for MDEs of 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 and 3.0 percentage points
